# Gang Conversion
The station has a crime problem, and it's about to get worse. A handful of crew have decided they'd rather carve out their own turf than clock in for another shift. Each gang boss answers to nobody but themselves, and they intend to make that stick - by force, if they have to.
Gang Conversion can appear on shifts with as few as 3 players. Two or more rival gangs form at once, so it's never just the crew against one antagonist: it's everyone against a turf war that might not stay contained to just the gangs.
## Objective
Control the most turf by the end of the shift. Turf is tracked continuously, so check in on it - a gang that's been winning all round can still be out-tagged in the last few minutes.
## Tattoo Gun
Only the boss starts with one. Land a melee hit on an eligible crew member and they're recruited on the spot - no warning, no choice. A mindshielded target can't be converted. Hitting a rival gang member instead flips them to your side, stripping any rank they held.
Eligible targets must be a living, humanoid crew member. Silicons and anyone already in your own gang can't be (re-)converted.
## Spray Tagger
Every gang member gets one. Use it on the floor to paint a tag in your gang's colour, claiming that spot as turf. Tagging over a rival's mark scrubs it out first. Tagging your own mark again does nothing - look for untagged or rival ground instead. It has a short cooldown between uses.
## Ranks
- [bold]Boss[/bold]: founded the gang. Starts with a tattoo gun and a spray tagger. Can promote any gang member to enforcer with a right-click verb. Losing the boss doesn't end the gang, but it can no longer promote anyone new. - [bold]Enforcer[/bold]: a boss's trusted lieutenant. Gets their own tattoo gun on promotion, so they can recruit too. - [bold]Ganger[/bold]: everyone else. Can tag turf, but can't recruit or promote.
## Winning
Turf is counted across the whole station on a timer, and again at the very end of the round. The gang with the most turf wins; ties are broken by whichever gang has the most living members. A gang that loses every member doesn't get removed from the board - their last tally still counts, they just can't grow it any further.
## Fighting the Gangs
- A mindshield operation makes someone immune to the tattoo gun. - Cleaning or painting over a gang tag removes it from their turf count, same as a rival gang tagging over it. - A gang with no boss and no enforcers left can't recruit new members, only hold or lose what they already have.
## Tips
- Tag early and tag often. A few seconds of spray paint is worth more than a long fight you might lose. - Don't let the boss wander off alone with the only tattoo gun in the gang - promote an enforcer early so a lucky hit on the boss doesn't end your recruiting for good. - Watch for rival taggers re-claiming ground the moment you look away.
